candidates.title: The Olympia & Sand Creek Ry.
candidates.excerpt: A time for a change So, you want to build a railroad, but perhaps you’re having a hard time finding a dedicated space for a layout. Or maybe you have the space, but you lack the ability to work well with small details, such as those found on N and HO scale models. And perhaps you’d like a large railroad, but you’re just overwhelmed by the cost in time and resources to build one. If any or all of those concerns fit your situation, then consider building a narrow gauge O scale sectional layout, such as my Olympia & Sand Creek Ry. The layout, also known as just “Olympia,” was constructed in three distinct sections over a 12-year period. Each section contained its own set of approachable projects, spreading the cost and modeling work over time. The railroad is built into furniture-like shadowboxes, giving the layout a museum-quality finish, which allows it to comfortably blend into the living spaces that also need to be used by others. candidates.excerpt: Schneider will make Norfolk Southern its primary eastern rail provider under an agreement announced Oct. 29 aimed at expanding domestic intermodal capacity and giving shippers more options to move freight across the eastern United States. The agreement, effective in November, shifts Schneider’s NYSE: SNDR) company-owned equipment, drivers and logistics operations away from CSX (NASDAQ: CSX) and pairs it with Norfolk Southern’s 22-state intermodal network. candidates.title: Kroll and StepStone launch private credit PIK indicators
candidates.excerpt: Kroll and StepStone launch private credit PIK indicators Kroll and StepStone Group have launched three new payment-in-kind (PIK) indicators to provide greater transparency into the use of non-cash interest in private credit markets. The indicators form part of the firms’ private credit benchmarks, covering more than 28,000 direct lending instruments, 18,000 deals and 13,000 borrowers, with historical data dating back to 2012. They measure PIK as a proportion of interest income, the percentage of loans with an active PIK component by deal count, and their share of outstanding principal. The indicators will also allow investors to compare PIK usage across geographies, sectors and borrower sizes. The launch comes as the firms’ data suggests PIK usage is moderating, with non-cash interest accounting for 2.86 per cent of interest income on loans originated globally over the previous 12 months, as of 10 October 2026.
